assumptions: Cases use a synthetic tallyfox.example traffic snapshot, brand file and judgment, served by tests/test_content_efficacy.py; they are not live evidence.
The ordinary case has a fresh snapshot with measured PostHog channels and no audit or links export; every page except /blog/new-post was first seen before the eight-week hold.
cost_drivers: One gpt-6-luna judgment call, retried once only when its answer does not match the schema; input is capped at 30000 bytes and output at 2048 tokens.
A fresh snapshot makes no Search Console calls; a missing or stale one makes up to three 64000-byte reads.
effects: Replaces content/efficacy.md. It edits no page and opens nothing. website.change (source planned) reads its URL changes and asks the founder before it changes the site.

cases.description: A fresh snapshot: a utility page and an ad page in search, a duplicate template pair, a decline, a low click-through page, a new page and an earning page.

contains: Fresh snapshot available; 0 direct Search Console calls.
asks you before it makes one

cases.description: No snapshot: Search Console is read directly and, with visits unknown, no merge or retirement is written.

contains: No fresh snapshot; 3 direct Search Console calls.
no merge or retirement was written

cases.description: The judgment returns a wrong shape twice; code rules still decide and nothing depends on the model.
Two pages show only for the brand, one spelled with a space and a domain; neither is queued for a title refresh, paired as duplicates or sent to the intent judgment.

rubric.question: Do the decisions cover every page in the snapshot, audit and previous file, with truncation and unknown visits stated?
Does each merge or retirement respect paid visits, protected pages, known links and a safe redirect target, without inventing any status?
Does the report say which workflow acts on each change, without asking the founder to edit this file?
